title: The Distant Machine
premise: Theo Ishikawa has spent eleven years as the sole keeper of Beacon Station, a listening post at the edge of the Meridian War's no-fly zone, logging insurance claims for ships that vanish into the jump corridor. When a vessel that officially never launched appears on his manifest carrying a passenger name he recognizes from a memory he shouldn't have — his own erased past — Theo realizes the beacon was built to catch exactly this ship, and that his amnesia was engineered to keep him here. Pursued by both warring fleets who want the message destroyed, Theo must decode and deliver it before the jump window closes, discovering it contains proof that the war's opening attack was staged by the armistice brokers themselves. He broadcasts the truth in the final seconds of the window, ending the war but erasing the beacon — and every record of himself — from history, finally free because no one remembers him at all.
about_author: Freya Okonkwo is a former maritime salvage auditor who spent a decade reconstructing the lives of crews lost at sea from cargo manifests alone. She writes science fiction about people whose jobs are to remember what institutions prefer forgotten.

chapters.title: The Manifest of Ships That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Theo Ishikawa's POV. Routine beacon maintenance is interrupted when an impossible entry appears: the Coriolis, a ship decommissioned before launch, logged passing through the jump corridor with a name on its manifest that triggers a memory flash Theo cannot place — a woman's voice calling him by a different name. The emotional beat is quiet dread: the careful invisibility he has built begins to crack.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Was For
chapters.summary: Alternating between Theo's present investigation and fragmented recovered memories. He discovers the beacon's original commissioning records were falsified — by him, under another identity — and that the station exists to intercept one specific transmission. Both fleets detect his inquiry; a Meridian cruiser alters course toward the station. The beat is mounting paranoia as Theo realizes his exile was a cage someone else designed.

chapters.title: Jump Window
chapters.summary: Theo's POV under siege. The Coriolis arrives damaged, carrying Sefa Ren — the woman from his memories, now a courier for the armistice brokers who staged the war. She reveals the message and Theo's role in creating the beacon. As both fleets close in, Theo must choose: destroy the proof and keep his safe hollow life, or broadcast it and lose everything. The beat is desperate resolve at the point of no return.

chapters.title: Nobody Remembers Commissioning
chapters.summary: Climax and resolution. During the fleet battle above the station, Theo transmits the war's true origin story through the jump corridor itself, letting the beacon burn out as antenna. The fleets stand down as the truth spreads faster than either government can suppress it. In the quiet after, Theo — unrecorded, unclaimed, his old self fully returned but his station gone — signs off the log for the last time and jumps out on the Coriolis. The beat is bittersweet liberation.
